drafted_from: tool:google-account-trash_mail_thread's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Move conversation 18c1a2b3d4e5f601 to Trash. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-trash_mail_thread as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Move conversation 18c1a2b3d4e5f601 to Trash." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-trash_mail_thread, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"thread_id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f601"}.
3. Read what comes back: the request goes as POST  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/threads/18c1a2b3d4e5f601/trash with no body.

worked_examples.title: Move a Gmail conversation to Trash on a sample input
worked_examples.given: read from tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (its invoke url, method and body_template) and checked against tools/read-and-write-gmail/test/rows.test.mjs. A conversation of three messages, id 18c1a2b3d4e5f601. The call it makes: POST the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/threads/18c1a2b3d4e5f601/trash with no body.
worked_examples.hands_back: Gmail answers {"id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f601"}; all three messages now carry TRASH. restore_mail_thread brings them back.
